examples.en: Don't hesitate like that, just say it quickly.
I didn't have the courage to confess, so I kept dithering.
I dawdled and missed the last bus.

examples.ko: 왜 질문에 대답도 못 하고 우물쭈물해요?
examples.en: Why are you hesitating instead of answering the question?
While I was dithering, all the seats got taken.

examples.ko: 메뉴를 못 골라서 직원 앞에서 우물쭈물하고 있었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't choose from the menu, so I was hesitating in front of the staff.

explain: '머뭇거리다'와 비슷하지만 '우물쭈물'은 말이나 행동을 분명하게 못 해서 답답해 보이는 느낌이 강해요. '우물쭈물 말을 얼버무리다'처럼 부사로도 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '머뭇거리다' (to hesitate), but '우물쭈물' strongly suggests being unclear and indecisive in a frustrating way. It is also often used as an adverb, as in '우물쭈물 말을 얼버무리다' (to mumble evasively).

examples.en: The wind was strong, so the umbrella rib broke.

examples.ko: 우산살 하나가 휘어서 잘 안 펴져요.
examples.en: One rib is bent, so the umbrella doesn't open well.
My finger got caught in the umbrella ribs and it hurt.
It's a new umbrella, but the ribs are already bent.

examples.ko: 우산살을 고쳐 주는 가게를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a shop that repairs umbrella ribs.

examples.ko: 이 우산은 우산살이 가늘어서 센 바람에 약해요.
examples.en: This umbrella has thin ribs, so it is weak against strong wind.

explain: 우산의 천을 받치는 가는 뼈대예요. 손잡이 쪽 긴 막대는 '우산대'라고 해서 구분해요.
explain_en: These are the thin frame bars that hold up the umbrella fabric. The long shaft on the handle side is called '우산대', so the two are different parts.

examples.ko: 우스개로 한 말인데 동생은 진지하게 들었어요.
examples.en: I said it as a joke, but my younger sibling took it seriously.

examples.ko: 회식 자리에서 부장님이 우스개 한마디를 던졌어요.
examples.en: At the company dinner, the manager threw in a joke.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 우스개를 잘 해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: He is good at telling jokes, so he's very popular.
This isn't a joke, I really mean it.

examples.ko: 우스개 삼아 한 말이니까 마음에 두지 마세요.
examples.en: I said it just for fun, so please don't take it to heart.

examples.ko: 친구의 우스개 덕분에 모두 크게 웃었어요.
examples.en: Thanks to my friend's joke, everyone laughed loudly.

explain: '우스개로 하는 말', '우스개 삼아'처럼 장난으로 가볍게 한 말이라는 느낌으로 많이 써요. '농담'은 '농담이야'처럼 진담이 아니라는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 '우스개'는 그런 쓰임이 적어요.
explain_en: It is often used in phrases like '우스개로 하는 말' and '우스개 삼아', meaning something said lightly for fun. '농담' can also be used like '농담이야' (I'm kidding), but '우스개' is rarely used that way.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 우스갯소리를 해서 사람들을 자주 웃겨요.
examples.en: My uncle often makes people laugh by telling jokes.
I said it as a joke, so please don't be angry.
The joke my grandfather told me was really funny.
I told a joke to lighten the mood.
That's just a joke, nothing more.

examples.ko: 요즘 인터넷에 도는 우스갯소리 들어 봤어요?
examples.en: Have you heard the joke going around the internet these days?

explain: '농담'은 '농담이야'처럼 진담이 아니라는 뜻으로도 쓰지만, '우스갯소리'는 웃기려고 하는 말이나 이야기에 더 가까워요. 줄여서 '우스개'라고도 해요.
explain_en: '농담' can mean 'I'm not serious' as in '농담이야', but '우스갯소리' is closer to a funny remark or story told to make people laugh. It can be shortened to '우스개'.

examples.en: I want to go on a space trip someday.
Space travel is still far too expensive.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 꿈은 우주여행을 하는 거였어요.
examples.en: My childhood dream was to travel into space.
If space travel becomes possible, will you go to the moon?

examples.ko: 아들은 우주여행 영화를 보고 우주비행사가 되고 싶어 해요.
examples.en: My son watched a space travel movie and now wants to be an astronaut.
I heard the training needed for space travel is really tough.

explain: '우주여행을 가다'와 '우주여행을 하다' 둘 다 자연스러워요. 아직은 영화, 뉴스, 미래 이야기에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
explain_en: Both '우주여행을 가다' and '우주여행을 하다' sound natural. It still appears mostly in movies, news and talk about the future.

examples.en: The sky is gloomy today.

examples.ko: 벽 색이 우중충해서 방이 어두워 보여요.
examples.en: The wall color is dull, so the room looks dark.
On gloomy days, my mood sinks too.
Isn't the color of the clothes too drab?
It's the rainy season, so the weather has been gloomy for days.

examples.ko: 우중충하던 골목이 밝은 벽화 덕분에 환해졌어요.
examples.en: The gloomy alley became bright thanks to a cheerful mural.

explain: 날씨뿐 아니라 방, 옷 색, 분위기가 어둡고 칙칙할 때도 써요. '칙칙하다'와 비슷하고 '화창하다'와 반대되는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It describes not only weather but also rooms, clothing colors or moods that look dark and dull. It is close to '칙칙하다' and is the opposite of '화창하다' (bright and sunny).

examples.en: The mailman brought me a package.
The postman delivers letters every day.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때 우체부가 되고 싶었어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I wanted to be a mailman.
I received the registered mail directly from the mailman.

examples.ko: 우체부가 오기 전에 우편함을 비워 두세요.
examples.en: Please empty the mailbox before the mailman comes.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에도 우체부는 열심히 일해요.
examples.en: Even on rainy days, the postman works hard.

explain: 공식적인 말로는 '집배원'이라고도 해요. 일상 대화에서는 '우체부 아저씨'처럼 아직도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: The more official term is '집배원'. In everyday talk, people still often say things like '우체부 아저씨'.

examples.en: My knee that I fell on is throbbing with pain.
My tooth is throbbing because of a cavity.

examples.ko: 밤새 상처가 욱신욱신해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: The wound throbbed all night, so I couldn't sleep.
After walking for a long time, my legs ache.
The wounded area throbs and feels hot.

examples.ko: 어제 운동한 뒤로 어깨가 욱신욱신 아파요.
examples.en: My shoulder has been aching since I worked out yesterday.

explain: 찌르듯이 계속 쑤시는 아픔을 나타내요. 동사 '욱신거리다'나 '욱신욱신하다'로도 자주 말하고, '쑤시다'와 함께 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It describes a pain that keeps stabbing or throbbing. It is also often used as the verbs '욱신거리다' or '욱신욱신하다', and it goes well with '쑤시다' (to ache).

examples.ko: 이번 납품가에는 포장비와 운송비가 모두 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This delivery price includes both packaging and shipping costs.
Shipping costs more when you send it overseas.

examples.ko: 무게가 무거워서 운송비를 따로 내야 해요.
examples.en: It's heavy, so I have to pay the transport cost separately.
I brought it myself to save on transport costs.

examples.ko: 일정 금액 이상 사면 운송비는 무료예요.
examples.en: If you spend over a certain amount, shipping is free.

examples.ko: 이 가격에 운송비는 포함되어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: Transport cost is not included in this price.

explain: 인터넷 쇼핑에서는 '배송비'라는 말을 더 많이 써요. '운송비'는 큰 짐이나 물건을 옮기는 데 드는 돈을 말할 때 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In online shopping, '배송비' is used more often. '운송비' often appears when talking about the cost of moving large goods or cargo.

en: operating difficulties; trouble keeping an organization running

examples.ko: 손님이 줄어서 가게가 운영난을 겪고 있어요.
examples.en: Customers have decreased, so the shop is struggling to stay open.

examples.ko: 그 학교는 운영난 때문에 문을 닫게 됐어요.
examples.en: That school ended up closing because of financial difficulties.
Small libraries are suffering from funding troubles.
As the financial trouble got worse, the staff took pay cuts.

examples.ko: 병원이 운영난으로 어려움을 겪는다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news that the hospital is having trouble due to management difficulties.

examples.ko: 회사가 운영난을 이기려고 새 상품을 내놨어요.
examples.en: The company released a new product to overcome its management difficulties.

explain: 뉴스에서 가게, 학교, 병원, 도서관 소식에 자주 나오는 말이에요. '운영난을 겪다', '운영난에 시달리다', '운영난이 심해지다'처럼 써요. '구인난', '취업난'도 같은 '-난' 말이에요.
explain_en: It often appears in news about shops, schools, hospitals and libraries. It is used as '운영난을 겪다', '운영난에 시달리다' and '운영난이 심해지다'. '구인난' and '취업난' are other words ending in '-난'.

examples.ko: 바자회에서 번 돈으로 봉사단 운영비를 마련하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to raise the volunteer group's operating costs with the money from the bazaar.

examples.ko: 가게 운영비가 매달 너무 많이 들어요.
examples.en: The shop's running costs are too high every month.

examples.ko: 정부가 작은 단체에 운영비를 지원해 줘요.
examples.en: The government supports small organizations with operating costs.
We moved the office to cut operating costs.
Most of the club fees are spent on operating costs.
Operating costs include electricity bills and salaries.

explain: 가게, 학교, 단체를 계속 이어 가는 데 드는 돈이에요. '운영비를 마련하다', '운영비를 지원하다', '운영비를 줄이다'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is the money needed to keep a shop, school or group running. People commonly say '운영비를 마련하다' (raise), '운영비를 지원하다' (support) and '운영비를 줄이다' (cut).

examples.en: The child cried and threw a tantrum, so it was hard.
She made a big scene, weeping and wailing that she didn't want to part.

examples.ko: 울고불고 매달리는 동생을 두고 갈 수가 없었어요.
examples.en: I couldn't leave my younger sibling clinging to me in tears.

examples.ko: 울고불고 하소연해 봤지만 아무도 들어 주지 않았어요.
examples.en: I pleaded in tears, but nobody listened.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 주사를 맞을 때마다 울고불고 소리를 질러요.
examples.en: That child cries and screams every time he gets a shot.

examples.ko: 울고불고 싸우던 형제가 어느새 같이 놀고 있어요.
examples.en: The brothers who were fighting in tears are already playing together.

explain: 그냥 우는 것이 아니라 소리치고 야단을 피우며 우는 모습이에요. '울고불고 난리다', '울고불고 매달리다'처럼 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes not just crying but crying loudly and making a fuss. It is often used in phrases like '울고불고 난리다' (making a huge scene) and '울고불고 매달리다' (cling in tears).

en: cry and scream; yell in tears

examples.en: The child cries and screams for me to buy a toy.
Yesterday I wept and wailed over the breakup.
Don't cry and scream, let's talk calmly.
I held the screaming, crying child and soothed her.
No matter how much you cry and wail, it's already too late.
The actors cried and wailed as they performed, and I teared up.

explain: 소리 내어 울면서 야단을 피울 때 써요. 큰 소리로 우는 모습을 말하니까 조용히 눈물만 흘릴 때는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it when someone cries out loud and makes a fuss. Since it describes loud crying, it doesn't fit when someone just quietly sheds tears.

examples.en: Every morning, the sound of church bells rings in from afar.
Piano sounds drift over from next door.
The sound of drums began to ring out from beyond the mountain.
Every night, singing echoed from somewhere.
When the announcement rang out, people stood up.

examples.ko: 가슴 깊은 곳에서 뭉클한 감동이 울려오는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: It felt as if a deep emotion was resonating from deep in my heart.

explain: 소리가 퍼져서 나 쪽으로 다가올 때 써요. '들려오다'와 비슷하지만 '울려오다'는 소리가 울리면서 전해지는 느낌이 있어요. 소리뿐 아니라 마음에 느낌이 전해질 때도 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a sound spreads and reaches you. It is similar to '들려오다' (to be heard), but '울려오다' has the feel of a sound resonating as it travels. It can also be used when a feeling is felt in the heart.

examples.ko: 점수에 인색한 심사위원 때문에 참가자들이 울상이었어요.
examples.en: The contestants looked ready to cry because of the stingy judge.
My younger sibling has a long face because there's so much homework.
Don't make a sad face, try smiling.

examples.ko: 시험 결과를 보고 친구가 울상이 됐어요.
examples.en: My friend looked about to cry after seeing the exam result.

examples.ko: 우산이 없는 사람들이 울상으로 서 있었어요.
examples.en: People without umbrellas stood there with sad faces.

examples.ko: 아침부터 울상인 걸 보니 무슨 일 있어요?
examples.en: You look about to cry since this morning. Did something happen?

explain: 실제로 울지는 않지만 곧 울 것 같은 얼굴이에요. '울상을 짓다', '울상이 되다', '울상이다'로 자주 써요.
explain_en: It means a face that looks as if the person is about to cry, though they aren't actually crying. It is commonly used as '울상을 짓다', '울상이 되다' and '울상이다'.

examples.en: It's cold, so my shoulders hunch up on their own.
I was startled by the loud noise and shrank back.
I keep losing my nerve because of the presentation.
I always end up shrinking in front of the teacher.
It's natural to shrink back from fear of failure.

examples.ko: 경기가 안 좋아서 소비가 움츠러들고 있어요.
examples.en: The economy is bad, so spending is shrinking.

explain: 몸이 오므라들 때뿐 아니라 마음이나 기운이 작아질 때도 써요. 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '움츠러드는', '움츠러드니까'가 돼요. 스스로 몸을 오므리는 동작은 '움츠리다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used both when the body curls up and when courage or energy shrinks. The 'ㄹ' drops in forms like '움츠러드는' and '움츠러드니까'. The deliberate action of pulling your body in is '움츠리다'.

examples.en: I paid extra to get the ticket.
Popular items are traded with a premium added.

examples.ko: 원래 가격에 웃돈을 얹어서 팔고 있어요.
examples.en: They are selling it with a markup on the original price.
You have to pay extra if you want it quickly.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 웃돈 없이는 살 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't buy this bag without paying a premium.

examples.ko: 중고 시장에서 웃돈 주고 사는 사람이 많아요.
examples.en: Many people pay a premium in the secondhand market.

explain: 정해진 값 말고 더 얹어 주는 돈이에요. '웃돈을 주다', '웃돈을 얹다', '웃돈이 붙다'처럼 말해요. '윗돈'이 아니라 '웃돈'이라고 써요.
explain_en: It is money added on top of the set price. People say '웃돈을 주다', '웃돈을 얹다' and '웃돈이 붙다'. The correct spelling is '웃돈', not '윗돈'.

examples.en: The teacher generously laughed off the child's mistake.
I just laughed off my friend's teasing.

examples.ko: 그 정도 실수는 웃어넘길 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can laugh off a mistake like that.
You shouldn't laugh off serious matters.

examples.ko: 그는 내 질문을 웃어넘기고 대답하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He laughed off my question and didn't answer.

examples.ko: 사소한 일은 그냥 웃어넘기는 편이 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to just laugh off small things.

explain: 문제를 심각하게 받아들이지 않고 웃으면서 지나갈 때 써요. 너그럽게 넘어간다는 좋은 뜻도 있고, 해야 할 말을 피한다는 느낌도 있어서 상황에 따라 달라져요.
explain_en: Use it when someone passes over a problem with a laugh instead of taking it seriously. It can mean being generous and easygoing, or it can feel like dodging something that should be addressed, depending on the situation.

examples.ko: 날씨가 추우니까 웃옷을 하나 더 입어요.
examples.en: It's cold, so put on one more outer layer.
Take off your jacket and hang it on the chair.
I got rained on, and my jacket is all wet.
This jacket goes well with the pants.
It was hot, so I worked with my outer layer off.
I put the key in my jacket pocket.

explain: 맨 겉에 입는 옷을 말해요. 바지나 치마와 짝이 되는 '윗옷(상의)'과 철자가 달라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 일상에서는 '겉옷'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means the outermost garment you wear. It is easy to confuse with '윗옷' (a top, as opposed to pants or a skirt) because the spelling differs. In daily speech people also often say '겉옷'.

examples.en: Laughter bloomed in every household.

examples.ko: 예쁘게 차려입은 아가씨들이 잔디밭에서 웃음꽃을 피우고 있어요.
examples.en: Nicely dressed young women are laughing merrily on the lawn.
When the family gets together, the laughter never stops.

examples.ko: 따뜻한 차를 마시며 웃음꽃 핀 대화를 나눴어요.
examples.en: We had a cheerful chat over warm tea.

examples.ko: 아이들 덕분에 우리 집은 웃음꽃이 가득해요.
examples.en: Thanks to the kids, our home is full of laughter.
At the reunion, we filled the air with laughter over old stories.

explain: 웃음이 꽃처럼 활짝 퍼지는 모습을 말해요. '피다'나 '피우다'와 함께 써서 '웃음꽃이 피다', '웃음꽃을 피우다'가 돼요. 여럿이 즐겁게 이야기하는 분위기에 어울려요.
explain_en: It pictures laughter spreading like blooming flowers. It is used with '피다' or '피우다', as in '웃음꽃이 피다' and '웃음꽃을 피우다'. It suits a lively mood of several people enjoying a chat.

examples.en: The classroom burst into laughter at the teacher's mistake.

examples.ko: 사회자의 농담 하나에 행사장이 웃음바다가 되었어요.
examples.en: One joke from the host sent the whole hall into laughter.
His story had the whole restaurant roaring with laughter.

examples.ko: 결혼식 영상이 나오자 순식간에 웃음바다로 변했어요.
examples.en: When the wedding video played, it turned into a sea of laughter in an instant.
The performance ended amid roars of laughter.

examples.ko: 갑자기 의자가 부서져서 모임이 웃음바다가 돼 버렸어요.
examples.en: The chair suddenly broke, and the meeting dissolved into laughter.

explain: '웃음바다가 되다'로 가장 많이 써요. 여러 사람이 한꺼번에 크게 웃을 때 쓰고, 혼자 웃는 상황에는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: It is used most often as '웃음바다가 되다'. It fits when many people laugh loudly at the same time, and doesn't suit a situation where only one person is laughing.

examples.en: It was hot, so the man had his shirt off.

examples.ko: 웃통을 벗고 수영장에 들어가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You can't go into the pool with your top off.
The kids are running around with no shirts on.

examples.ko: 공사장 인부가 웃통을 벗고 일하고 있어요.
examples.en: A construction worker is working with his shirt off.
After exercising, my upper body was soaked with sweat.

examples.ko: 그는 웃통도 가리지 않고 현관에 나왔어요.
examples.en: He came to the door without even covering his upper body.

explain: 몸의 윗부분, 특히 옷을 입는 상체를 말해요. '웃통을 벗다'로 가장 많이 쓰고, 편하게 하는 말이라 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the upper part of the body, especially the torso where you wear clothes. It is mostly used as '웃통을 벗다' (take one's shirt off) and is casual speech, so it is not used in formal settings.

examples.en: It's an old house, so the drafts are bad.
Cold air comes in through the window gaps, so it's chilly.
I put plastic on the window to block the draft.

examples.ko: 방은 따뜻한데 웃풍 때문에 코가 시려요.
examples.en: The room is warm, but my nose is cold because of the draft.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 웃풍이 센 방에서 자기 힘들어요.
examples.en: In winter, it's hard to sleep in a room with a strong draft.
I want to move to a house without drafts.

explain: 겨울에 문틈이나 창틈으로 방 안에 스며드는 찬 바람이에요. '웃풍이 세다', '웃풍이 들어오다', '웃풍을 막다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is the cold air that seeps into a room through gaps in doors or windows in winter. People say '웃풍이 세다' (a strong draft), '웃풍이 들어오다' and '웃풍을 막다'.

en: hum; make a noise; be noisy

examples.en: People are murmuring in the street over there.
When the accident happened, onlookers started buzzing.
I can hear a murmuring sound outside the classroom.
As the lecture was delayed, the students began to murmur.

examples.ko: 복도가 너무 웅성거려서 집중이 안 돼요.
examples.en: The hallway is so noisy that I can't concentrate.

examples.ko: 무대에 불이 꺼지자 관객들이 웅성거리다가 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: When the stage lights went out, the audience buzzed and then went quiet.

explain: 여러 사람이 낮은 소리로 두런두런 떠들 때 써요. '시끄럽다'와 달리 말소리가 뒤섞여 들리는 느낌이고, 부사 '웅성웅성'으로도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when many people talk together in low voices. Unlike '시끄럽다' (loud), it suggests overlapping voices blending into a murmur, and the adverb '웅성웅성' is also common.

examples.en: Write following the rules for using manuscript paper.
In elementary school, I wrote my diary on manuscript paper.

examples.ko: 원고지 열 장 분량으로 써 오세요.
examples.en: Please write about ten sheets' worth of manuscript paper.

examples.ko: 원고지는 한 칸에 한 글자씩 써요.
examples.en: On manuscript paper, you write one character per square.
I ran out of manuscript paper, so I bought more.
These days I write on a computer rather than on manuscript paper.

explain: 글쓰기 숙제나 시험에서 분량을 '원고지 10매'처럼 말해요. 종이를 세는 말은 '매'나 '장'을 써요.
explain_en: In writing assignments and tests, length is often given like '원고지 10매' (ten sheets of manuscript paper). Sheets are counted with '매' or '장'.

examples.en: A can is shaped like a cylinder.
I solved a problem about finding the volume of a cylinder.
A cylinder has round top and bottom faces.
This container looks like a cylinder.
If you lay a cylinder on its side, it rolls easily.
In math class, we made a cylinder out of paper.

explain: 수학 시간에 주로 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '통 모양'이라고 말하기도 해요. 같이 배우는 도형으로 '원뿔', '각기둥'이 있어요.
explain_en: It is mostly a math-class word; in daily life people may say '통 모양' (tube shape). Shapes studied alongside it include '원뿔' (cone) and '각기둥' (prism).

examples.en: I'm glad the problem was resolved smoothly.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 서로 양보해서 원만히 합의했어요.
examples.en: The two compromised and reached an amicable agreement.
I try to get along well with my neighbors.
Today's meeting ended without a hitch.
I'm happy we wrapped up the contract smoothly.

examples.ko: 갈등을 원만히 풀려면 서로 이야기를 들어야 해요.
examples.en: To settle a conflict amicably, you have to listen to each other.

explain: 다투지 않고 둥글게 잘 풀릴 때 써요. '해결하다', '지내다', '합의하다'와 자주 쓰이고, '원만하게'라고도 해요.
explain_en: Use it when things go well without conflict. It is often used with '해결하다' (resolve), '지내다' (get along) and '합의하다' (agree), and can also be said as '원만하게'.

examples.en: An ice cream cone is cone-shaped.
Measure the height of the cone.
The party hat is pointy like a cone.
A cone has just one circle as its base.
I rolled up the paper to make a cone.

examples.ko: 도로 위의 원뿔 표지가 눈에 잘 띄어요.
examples.en: The cone markers on the road are easy to spot.

explain: 수학에서 쓰는 도형 이름이에요. 도로 공사 때 세우는 빨간 '라바콘'은 일상에서 그렇게 말하지만 모양은 원뿔과 비슷해요.
explain_en: It is the math name for the cone shape. The red traffic cones used in road work are commonly called '라바콘' in daily life, though their shape is similar to a cone.

examples.ko: 이 섬에는 아직 원시림이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: This island still has primeval forest.
Walking in the virgin forest felt mysterious.
A campaign to protect the primeval forest was held.
Many rare animals live in the virgin forest.

examples.ko: 개발 때문에 원시림이 빠르게 사라지고 있어요.
examples.en: Because of development, the primeval forest is disappearing fast.
We followed the path that crosses the virgin forest.

explain: 사람 손을 타지 않은 자연 그대로의 숲이에요. '밀림'은 나무가 빽빽하게 우거진 숲이고, '원시림'은 손을 안 댄 숲이라는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is a forest left in its natural state, untouched by people. '밀림' is a dense, thickly overgrown forest, while '원시림' stresses that it hasn't been disturbed.

examples.en: We made a fire using a primitive method.

examples.ko: 그 시절에는 원시적 도구로 농사를 지었어요.
examples.en: In those days, people farmed with primitive tools.

examples.ko: 이건 너무 원시적 방식이라 시간이 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: This is such a primitive way of doing it that it takes a long time.

examples.ko: 주말에 원시적 생활을 체험하는 캠프에 갔어요.
examples.en: On the weekend, I went to a camp that lets you experience a primitive lifestyle.

examples.ko: 원시적 감각이 살아 있는 그림이라 인상적이에요.
examples.en: It's an impressive painting with a raw, primal feeling.
I saw an instrument of primitive form at the museum.

explain: 뒤에 명사가 와서 '원시적 방법'처럼 쓰거나 '원시적인', '원시적이다' 형태로도 많이 말해요. 옛날 모습이라는 뜻 말고, 방법이 낡고 뒤떨어졌다고 놀리는 말로도 써요.
explain_en: It can come before a noun as in '원시적 방법', and it is also very common as '원시적인' or '원시적이다'. Besides meaning 'of ancient times', it can be used to tease that a method is outdated and backward.

examples.ko: 책을 읽고 나면 원위치에 꽂아 두세요.
examples.en: After reading a book, put it back where it was.
Please put the chairs back in their original position.
Check that everything is in its original place.
When cleaning is done, please tidy things back to their places.
Things got tangled, and we ended up back at square one.
The desks we moved go back to where they were after class.

explain: 일상에서는 '제자리'라는 말을 더 편하게 써요. '원위치'는 안내문이나 지시할 때 자주 나오고, '원위치로 돌아가다'는 일이 처음 상태로 돌아갔다는 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk, '제자리' sounds more casual. '원위치' often appears in notices and instructions, and '원위치로 돌아가다' can also mean that a situation has gone back to square one.

examples.en: Food packaging always lists the ingredients.
Check the ingredients of this snack.

examples.ko: 원재료 값이 올라서 제품 가격도 올랐어요.
examples.en: Raw material prices went up, so the product price rose too.
The main ingredients are flour and sugar.

examples.ko: 원재료에 알레르기 성분이 있는지 꼭 봐요.
examples.en: I always check whether the ingredients contain allergens.

examples.ko: 공장에 원재료가 도착하지 않아 생산이 멈췄어요.
examples.en: The raw materials didn't arrive at the factory, so production stopped.

explain: 식품 포장 뒷면에 '원재료명'이라고 적혀 있어서 자주 보는 말이에요. '재료'는 일반적인 말이고, '원재료'는 가공하기 전 처음 재료라는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: You often see this on the back of food packaging as '원재료명' (ingredient list). '재료' is the general word, while '원재료' feels like the starting materials before processing.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 원칙적으로 예약한 손님만 받아요.
examples.en: As a rule, this restaurant only takes customers with reservations.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 원칙적으로 직원의 부업을 금지해요.
examples.en: Our company prohibits employees from side jobs in principle.
In principle, refunds are only possible within a week.

examples.ko: 원칙적으로는 안 되지만 이번에는 특별히 허락할게요.
examples.en: It's not allowed in principle, but I'll make an exception this time.

examples.ko: 이 건물에는 원칙적으로 외부인이 들어올 수 없어요.
examples.en: As a rule, outsiders cannot enter this building.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 원칙적 입장은 같지만 세부 사항은 달라요.
examples.en: The two share the same basic position, but differ on the details.

explain: '원칙적으로'의 형태로 가장 많이 쓰고, 뒤에 '하지만', '예외는 있어요'처럼 예외를 말하는 경우가 많아요. 규칙이나 안내문, 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used most often as '원칙적으로', and it is often followed by an exception, as in '하지만' or '예외는 있어요'. It appears frequently in rules, notices and the news.

examples.en: The meeting is proceeding smoothly.
They adjusted the signals so that traffic flows smoothly.

examples.ko: 소통이 원활히 되려면 서로 잘 들어야 해요.
examples.en: For communication to go smoothly, you must listen well to each other.
The internet isn't connecting smoothly.
Please help everyone finish the event without a hitch.
Stretch often so that your blood circulates well.

explain: 일상에서는 '순조롭게'나 '잘'이라고 하고, '원활히'는 조금 격식 있는 말이에요. 소통, 교통, 진행, 공급처럼 막힘없이 흐르는 일에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '순조롭게' or '잘', and '원활히' is a bit more formal. It suits things that flow without blockage, such as communication, traffic, progress and supply.

examples.ko: 이 월간지는 매달 첫째 주에 나와요.
examples.en: This monthly magazine comes out in the first week of each month.
I have a regular subscription to a monthly magazine.
My photo was published in a monthly magazine.
I bought the fashion monthly to get the bonus gift.
I borrowed a back issue of the monthly magazine from the library.

examples.ko: 월간지 기사를 쓰는 일을 하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to work writing articles for a monthly magazine.

explain: 한 달에 한 번 나오는 잡지예요. 일주일에 한 번 나오면 '주간지', 석 달에 한 번이면 '계간지'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a magazine published once a month. One published weekly is a '주간지', and one published quarterly is a '계간지'.

examples.ko: 월급쟁이보다 자영업이 수입은 불안정하지만 더 자유로워요.
examples.en: Self-employment has less stable income than a salaried job, but it's freer.

examples.ko: 월급쟁이는 매달 같은 날 돈을 받아요.
examples.en: Salaried workers get paid on the same day every month.
My father lived as a salaried worker all his life.

examples.ko: 월급쟁이 생활이 힘들어서 가끔 창업을 꿈꿔요.
examples.en: Life as an office worker is hard, so I sometimes dream of starting a business.
It's not easy for a salaried worker to buy a house.
My office-worker friends are all just waiting for Friday.

explain: '직장인'은 중립적인 말이고, '월급쟁이'는 친근하거나 자조하는 느낌으로 말할 때가 많아요. 윗사람이나 모르는 사람에게는 '직장인'이 더 무난해요.
explain_en: '직장인' is the neutral word, while '월급쟁이' is often said in a friendly or self-deprecating tone. When talking to a superior or a stranger, '직장인' is safer.

examples.en: What is your average monthly income?
The monthly average temperature rose compared to last year.

examples.ko: 우리 가족의 월평균 식비는 오십만 원이에요.
examples.en: Our family's average monthly food expense is 500,000 won.
The monthly average number of users has passed 100,000.

examples.ko: 저는 월평균 세 권 정도 책을 읽어요.
examples.en: I read about three books a month on average.

examples.ko: 월평균 지출을 기록하면 돈을 아낄 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you record your monthly average spending, you can save money.

explain: 통계나 뉴스에서 많이 쓰는 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '한 달 평균'이라고도 말해요. 같은 방식으로 '연평균'이라는 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It is common in statistics and the news. In everyday talk you can also say '한 달 평균'. Following the same pattern, there is also the word '연평균' (yearly average).

en: well, what do you know; on the contrary

examples.ko: 비가 올 줄 알았는데 웬걸, 하루 종일 맑았어요.
examples.en: I thought it would rain, but no, it was sunny all day.

examples.ko: 쉬울 줄 알았는데 웬걸, 정말 어려웠어요.
examples.en: I thought it would be easy, but boy, it was really hard.
What, you've already finished it all?

examples.ko: 일찍 도착할 줄 알았는데 웬걸, 길이 너무 막혔어요.
examples.en: I thought I'd arrive early, but wow, the road was jammed.

examples.ko: 처음엔 안 먹겠다더니 웬걸, 세 그릇이나 먹었어요.
examples.en: He said he wouldn't eat at first, but would you believe it, he ate three bowls.
Not at all, it wasn't hard for me.

explain: 예상과 전혀 다른 결과가 나왔을 때 놀라서 하는 말이에요. 보통 '~줄 알았는데 웬걸,' 형태로 쓰고, '웬걸요'는 '천만에요'처럼 가볍게 부정할 때 써요.
explain_en: People say it in surprise when the result is completely different from what they expected. It is usually used in the pattern '~줄 알았는데 웬걸,' and '웬걸요' is used to lightly deny something, like 'not at all'.

examples.en: I can understand Korean reasonably well.
If you've done a fair amount, take a rest now.
My cold has gotten pretty much better.
Stop eating once you're reasonably full.

examples.ko: 웬만큼 친해지기 전에는 말을 편하게 안 놓아요.
examples.en: I don't speak casually until we've become reasonably close.

examples.ko: 요리는 웬만큼 할 줄 아니까 걱정 마세요.
examples.en: I know how to cook reasonably well, so don't worry.

explain: 형용사 '웬만하다'에서 온 부사로, 아주 잘은 아니어도 어느 정도 괜찮은 수준을 말해요. '웬만큼 해서는 안 돼요'처럼 부정과 함께 쓰면 '보통 수준으로는 부족하다'는 뜻이 돼요.
explain_en: This adverb comes from the adjective '웬만하다' and means to a fairly decent level, though not perfect. Used with negation, as in '웬만큼 해서는 안 돼요', it means that an ordinary level of effort isn't enough.
